notes: Both games are on-foot obstacle stages run at the player's own pace - a hallway swept by a timed blue and red grid line, then a chasm crossed by pairs of steps where one of each pair is an illusion - so Obby & Platformer leads, and its P6 is doing real work here: the step pairs have to be physically crossable or Gravity Fractures is unplayable. Party & Casual is named second for the round-based elimination format and the lobby of thirty competitors. Shape is course-flat, a two-stage course progressing horizontally through the cyber-bunker; I kept Classic Obby for its ordered platform track but dropped checkpoint-respawn, since the author eliminates rather than respawns, and traded its jump and moving obstacles for obstacle-timing on the sweeping grid phases and obstacle-guess on the solid-versus-holographic steps, with hazard-kill for the lasers that zap anything moving on red. With no user to ask I made the far end of Gravity Fractures the winner-zone, which is the finish the author stated, and I note that the hovering security drones have nowhere to land in this genre's table - they are hostile NPCs rather than ambient population, so they stay set dressing unless a spawner is added.
